rationale: Two actions. First, a bookkeeping correction: the interpretation recorded for a38031973bee49ac9248ded78a2843e4-question-1 concludes explained, so its disposition is set to explained instead of staying active. Second, converting the one concrete observation of this run into retained evidence: the readOnly probe that previously existed only as native feedback is now a fixed experiment executed by the controller in a clean copy. It supplies readOnly.recvAck with Context values the live instance's heartbeatCtx never emitted and records what maybeAdvance does - either a slice-bounds panic when the quorum position exceeds the outstanding request count, or confirmation of a read that the supplying voter never observed. The experiment is deliberately about an out-of-contract input: the recorded fact a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0 already establishes that no in-model producer supplies such a Context, so the comparison is expected to confirm the two behaviors without implying a CFT defect, and the interpretation keeps the refuted defect claim while replacing the earlier unreceipted probe with an executed one.

interpretations.rationale: Successor to the earlier revisions of this question, now with a retained execution instead of an unreceipted probe. Nothing in the source understanding changed: readOnly.recvAck still stores binary.LittleEndian.Uint64 of the peer-supplied Context as a read-position ack without any equality check against the positions the leader emitted, and maybeAdvance still slices unconfirmedReads by the quorum position without clamping. What changed is the evidence class: the fixed experiment runs in the clean copy and drives the unexported readOnly directly, admitting one stand-in read (oversized case) or two (forged case), self-acking with heartbeatCtx() as sendMsgReadIndexResponse does, injecting acks the leader never emitted, and then calling maybeAdvance with Voters[0]={1,2,3}. Its comparisons ask only what the code does under that input: (1) with a quorum of oversized ack positions the slice bound is exceeded and the call panics; (2) with a single forged ack at position 2, the leader self-ack plus that value is already a 2-of-3 quorum position, so both reads are confirmed although the forged voter never received a heartbeat carrying position 2. The controller owns the receipt and the comparison indices, so I do not cite them here. Still-applicable account retained from the previous revision: the premise that gives the earlier suspicion its force - a Context outside the set the live instance emitted - has no in-model producer, because readOnly is created only by raft.reset at a leadership transition, the sole writer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context is handleHeartbeat echoing the leader's own value, lower-term responses are dropped before dispatch, and heartbeatCtx emits a message total that write path only grows (a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0, 71f53a32a0c74532a55ad33bc1e71086-knowledge-1). Consequently the defect claim stays refuted for the crash-fault model: this is robustness against a peer or intermediary that fabricates or corrupts an 8-byte heartbeat context, which the CFT model excludes, and the experiment demonstrates the behavior rather than a reachable consensus defect. I deliberately did not invert the experiment into an in-model claim: the setup supplies the ack values itself, so no observation here bears on whether a legal producer exists. Remaining uncertainty is unchanged and unclaimed: addRequest does not deduplicate by request context, so documented ReadIndex retries with an identical context accumulate one unconfirmed entry and one heartbeat broadcast each while the leader cannot reach a quorum ack; I have not established that this is a reportable bounded-resource concern.

knowledge.assertion: recvAck stores the peer Context as a raw read position and maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads by the quorum position without validating the value
every legal Context producer echoes the live leader's emitted value, so the out-of-range precondition has no in-model trigger

limitations: The experiment injects ack values directly into the unexported readOnly, so its events characterise the code path under an out-of-contract input and do not establish network reachability.
The comparison outcomes and receipt identity are assigned by the controller; this account does not cite parsed indices and must be read together with that receipt.
The refutation of the in-model premise remains a source argument (lifetime and producer enumeration), not an executed one.

scope.description: Exercise the unexported readOnly confirmation path of package raft with ack values the live instance's heartbeatCtx never emitted, and record the two candidate consequences: an out-of-range slice in maybeAdvance, and confirmation of reads that the acking voter never observed.
assumptions: ack positions are supplied directly to readOnly.recvAck, standing in for MsgHeartbeatResp.Context values; this is an out-of-contract input, since the library's own follower path echoes the leader's context (see a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0).
ReadOnlySafe option; three voters (1,2,3) so the quorum position is the median of the stored acks.
The self-ack of the leader (id 1) is produced by heartbeatCtx() exactly as sendMsgReadIndexResponse does it.
excluded: Any claim that a legal cluster produces these inputs; the experiment characterises the code, not reachability.
Lease-based reads, which do not use the ack map.

experiment.prefix: Each test builds a fresh readOnly via newReadOnly(ReadOnlySafe), admits one or two MsgReadIndex stand-ins through readOnly.addRequest(committedIndex, msg), self-acks with readOnly.recvAck(leaderID, readOnly.heartbeatCtx()), then injects peer acks with readOnly.recvAck(peerID, littleEndianUint64(position)) using values the leader never emitted, and finally calls readOnly.maybeAdvance(quorum.JointConfig with Voters[0]={1,2,3}). No raft instance, network or storage is involved; the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads are read directly, and the maybeAdvance call in the oversized case is wrapped in a recover to record whether it panics.

comparisons.description: When the quorum ack position exceeds the number of outstanding read requests, maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads out of range and panics.
One forged ack value combined with the leader's self-ack reaches a 2-of-3 quorum position, so both admitted reads are confirmed although voter 3 never received a heartbeat carrying position 2.

knowledge.assertion: no in-model producer supplies a Context the live leader never emitted, which is why this experiment uses an out-of-contract input
